title: Quiz: Process Variation — Sources and Types

questions.text: A filling machine consistently produces volumes between 498 ml and 502 ml with no identifiable cause. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Variation that is always present, due to many small unknown factors, and predictable is common-cause variation. The process is 'in control' — no single cause can be identified.

questions.text: An API suddenly starts returning error codes because a cloud provider updated their authentication method. Which 6M category caused this variation?
questions.explanation: The cloud provider's change is an external Environmental factor. The change happened outside the team's direct control and altered the operating conditions of the process.

questions.text: Special-cause variation can be reduced by changing the fundamental design of the process.
questions.explanation: Special-cause variation is eliminated by identifying and removing the specific assignable cause. Changing the fundamental process design addresses common-cause variation, which is a management-level decision.

questions.text: The 5 Whys technique is used to:
options: Trace a defect back to its root cause
questions.explanation: The 5 Whys is a root-cause analysis technique. By repeatedly asking 'why?' you move past symptoms to the underlying root cause of a problem.

questions.text: In a Big Data pipeline, corrupted records arriving from an upstream source would be classified as a 'Material' variation in the 6M framework.
questions.explanation: In the 6M framework, 'Material' refers to the inputs to the process — in a data pipeline, this is the data itself. Corrupted or poor-quality input data is a Material variation source.
